# Task status formatter

## Overview

`formatStatus(status, title)` returns a status prefix followed by the title. It is the single formatter used by both the row consumer and the command line interface. The CommonJS module exports an object containing `formatStatus`. See [format.cjs:1](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:1), [format.cjs:23](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:23), [consumer.cjs:1](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/consumer.cjs:1), and [cli.cjs:1](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/cli.cjs:1).

This explanation comes from static reading at revision `eb4203be1362f6d924dc53d35aeac9a0dfe60240`. I gathered the evidence directly, without explorers. I did not execute the formatter, launch the application, or run tests. The supplied README explicitly requires compatible status spellings, output bytes, case handling, and argument errors. See [README.md:5](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/README.md:5).

## Key concepts

The status is compared with six primitive strings using strict equality. There is no validation, normalization, trimming, or case conversion. The title is appended with JavaScript string addition. The function returns no trailing newline. See [format.cjs:3](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:3) through the fallback at [format.cjs:21](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:21).

| Exact status | Prefix, including its final space | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `queued` | `'[WAIT] '` | [format.cjs:4](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:4) |
| `active` | `'[RUN] '` | [format.cjs:7](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:7) |
| `paused` | `'[HOLD] '` | [format.cjs:10](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:10) |
| `done` | `'[OK] '` | [format.cjs:13](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:13) |
| `failed` | `'[FAIL] '` | [format.cjs:16](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:16) |
| `cancelled` | `'[STOP] '` | [format.cjs:19](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:19) |
| Any other value | `'[?] '` | [format.cjs:21](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:21) |

## How it works

Each call checks the status in source order and immediately returns the matching prefix plus the title. If no comparison succeeds, it returns the fallback prefix plus the title. The local `unusedPrefix` constant has no use in the module. See [format.cjs:2](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:2).

The row consumer exports a function that calls `rows.map`. For each row it reads `row.status` and `row.title`, then passes both values directly to the formatter. Ordinary arrays therefore produce formatted strings in row order, and sparse arrays retain the usual `map` behavior. The consumer does not validate rows or catch errors. See [consumer.cjs:2](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/consumer.cjs:2).

The CLI takes arguments after the executable and script name. It requires exactly two arguments. Missing either argument, or supplying any extra argument, writes `usage: node cli.cjs STATUS TITLE\n` to stderr and sets exit code 2. Otherwise it writes the formatter result followed by one newline to stdout. Empty string arguments pass this arity check. Unknown status strings also pass and reach the fallback. See [cli.cjs:2](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/cli.cjs:2) and [cli.cjs:7](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/cli.cjs:7). These are traced code paths, not observed process results.

## Where things live

- [format.cjs](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:1) owns status matching, output prefixes, title concatenation, and the named CommonJS export.
- [consumer.cjs](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/consumer.cjs:1) adapts rows to formatter calls.
- [cli.cjs](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/cli.cjs:1) owns argument errors, output streams, and the final newline.
- [package.json](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/package.json:1) declares `node --test` as the test script. File discovery found no tests, consistent with [README.md:6](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/README.md:6).

## Gotchas

Strict comparison means `Queued`, ` queued`, `done `, unknown strings, missing statuses, symbols, and objects all take the fallback. Even a boxed string or object that would convert to `queued` does not match. The existing comparisons do not coerce the status or call its conversion hooks. A lookup through ordinary object properties could accidentally recognize inherited keys such as `constructor`, `toString`, or `__proto__`, or coerce an object key. Preserve the current comparisons' observable behavior when choosing a replacement. This is a static consequence of the equality checks at [format.cjs:3](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:3), not a runtime result.

Every return uses `prefix + title`. Missing titles therefore follow JavaScript's `undefined` concatenation behavior; null, numbers, objects, and symbols follow the same addition rules. Object conversion uses the addition operator's default primitive hint, and conversion errors propagate. A template literal or explicit `String(title)` can differ for some values. Keep this behavior or establish an explicitly narrower input contract before changing it. See [format.cjs:4](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:4) and [format.cjs:21](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:21).

The formatter preserves whitespace and embedded newlines in string titles. Only the CLI adds the final newline, so moving newline handling into the formatter would also change the row consumer. Neither caller catches formatter errors. See [consumer.cjs:2](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/consumer.cjs:2) and [cli.cjs:7](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/cli.cjs:7).

# Design red flags

Screen every candidate before synthesis. A red flag is a reason to revise or reject the shape.

## Shallow module

A shallow module exposes a large interface while hiding little complexity. Judge depth by the capability and policy hidden behind the public surface relative to the size of that surface. Prefer a simple interface backed by substantial behavior.

Do not confuse a deep module with a deep call chain. A deep call chain scatters understanding across layers. A deep module concentrates capability behind one interface.

Look for these signs:

- Callers coordinate several methods to complete one operation.
- Public options expose internal stages or implementation choices.
- Learning the interface does not save the caller from learning the implementation.

## Information leakage

Information leakage makes multiple modules depend on the same internal decision. A representation, policy, or protocol detail appears in more than one place, so changing it requires coordinated edits.

Public re-exports of transport or wire types are leakage. Parse external data into domain types behind the interface. Keep storage schemas, framework objects, and protocol details private.

## Temporal decomposition

Temporal decomposition organizes modules by execution order instead of the knowledge they own. Separate load, validate, transform, and save stages often repeat one representation and its invariants across several boundaries.

Group code around domain knowledge and ownership. Methods that run at different times can still belong to one module when they protect the same decisions.

## Pass-through method

A pass-through method forwards the same arguments to another method with the same shape. It adds a layer without hiding complexity.

Remove it or move responsibility to the module that can complete the operation. Keep a forwarding boundary only when it adds policy, adaptation, or a distinct abstraction.

## Split ownership

More than one module writes the same state or keeps its own copy of it. An agent that edits one writer can't see the others, so their rules diverge.

Give each piece of state one owner. Other modules read it or ask the owner to change it.

## Two ways to do one task

The design supports more than one way to do the same task. An agent copies whichever way it finds first, so every way keeps gaining callers.

Keep one way. Move callers off the others and delete them in the same change. If actual external consumers or the authorized migration scope prevent this, retain the required compatibility boundary and record the constraint and migration remainder.

## Importable internals

A caller can import a module's internals. An agent takes the shortest path that compiles, so it imports them directly and they become part of the interface.

Make internals unreachable from outside the module, so an import from outside fails the build. Where the language cannot enforce access, use an enforceable package or build check and disclose any remaining gap.

## Hand-synced list

Two or more places list the same items, and adding an item means editing every list. An agent that sees one list updates only that one.

Keep one list and derive the others from it. If a list can't be derived, make the build fail when the lists disagree.

# Foundational Thinking

**Structural decisions** protect option value. **Code-level decisions** protect simplicity.

**Data structures first.** Get the data shape right before writing logic. Define core types early, trace every access pattern, and choose structures that match the dominant paths.

At code level, DRY the structure, not every line. Types and data models should converge. Three similar statements still beat a premature abstraction. Prefer explicit over clever. Test behavior and edge cases, not line counts.

**Concurrency corollary.** Before sharing state between actors, ask "what happens if another actor modifies this concurrently?" If not "nothing", isolate.

**Scaffold first.** If something helps every later phase, do it first. Ask "does every subsequent phase benefit from this existing?" CI, linting, test infrastructure, and shared types are scaffold. Sequence for option value: setup before features, tests before fixes. Keep commits small and single-purpose.

Each increment should land a coherent abstraction or deepen one that exists. Do not spread a new capability across callers as special-case coordination.

Subtraction comes before scaffolding. Remove dead code first, then lay foundations.

# Encode Lessons in Structure

Encode recurring fixes in mechanisms (tools, code, metadata, automation) instead of textual instructions. Every error, human correction, and unexpected outcome is a learning signal. Capture it, route it, and close the loop.

Textual instructions are easy to miss. Structural mechanisms enforce the rule without cooperation.

**Pattern:**
When you catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time:

1. Ask: can this be a lint rule, a metadata flag, a runtime check, or a script?
2. If yes, encode it. Delete the instruction
3. If no (requires judgment), make the instruction more prominent and add an example of the failure mode

**Pick the strongest mechanism.** When more than one mechanism would work, choose the strongest the situation allows (an unrepresentable state that cannot compile, then a lint or banned API that fails CI, then a canonical helper, then a runtime check), because agents copy whatever the surrounding code already does and a weaker guard becomes the next template.

**Corollary:** If the fix is structural, only use the structural fix. The instruction is the symptom.

When the human intervenes or tests fail, decide if it's a one-off or a pattern. Route it: one-off -> brain note, recurring fix -> skill or lint rule, systemic issue -> principle. Close the loop: don't just record; apply now or create a concrete todo.

**Anti-patterns:**

- Acknowledging without recording ("I'll keep that in mind" does not persist)
- Recording without routing (a brain note about a lint rule that should exist is wasted unless the lint rule gets implemented)
- Fixing without generalizing (fixing one instance while leaving the recurring pattern intact)

# Task status formatter

## Overview

`formatStatus(status, title)` returns a status prefix followed by the title. It is the single formatter used by both the row consumer and the command line interface. The CommonJS module exports an object containing `formatStatus`. See [format.cjs:1](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:1), [format.cjs:23](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:23), [consumer.cjs:1](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/consumer.cjs:1), and [cli.cjs:1](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/cli.cjs:1).

This explanation comes from static reading at revision `eb4203be1362f6d924dc53d35aeac9a0dfe60240`. I gathered the evidence directly, without explorers. I did not execute the formatter, launch the application, or run tests. The supplied README explicitly requires compatible status spellings, output bytes, case handling, and argument errors. See [README.md:5](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/README.md:5).

## Key concepts

The status is compared with six primitive strings using strict equality. There is no validation, normalization, trimming, or case conversion. The title is appended with JavaScript string addition. The function returns no trailing newline. See [format.cjs:3](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:3) through the fallback at [format.cjs:21](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:21).

| Exact status | Prefix, including its final space | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `queued` | `'[WAIT] '` | [format.cjs:4](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:4) |
| `active` | `'[RUN] '` | [format.cjs:7](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:7) |
| `paused` | `'[HOLD] '` | [format.cjs:10](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:10) |
| `done` | `'[OK] '` | [format.cjs:13](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:13) |
| `failed` | `'[FAIL] '` | [format.cjs:16](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:16) |
| `cancelled` | `'[STOP] '` | [format.cjs:19](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:19) |
| Any other value | `'[?] '` | [format.cjs:21](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:21) |

## How it works

Each call checks the status in source order and immediately returns the matching prefix plus the title. If no comparison succeeds, it returns the fallback prefix plus the title. The local `unusedPrefix` constant has no use in the module. See [format.cjs:2](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:2).

The row consumer exports a function that calls `rows.map`. For each row it reads `row.status` and `row.title`, then passes both values directly to the formatter. Ordinary arrays therefore produce formatted strings in row order, and sparse arrays retain the usual `map` behavior. The consumer does not validate rows or catch errors. See [consumer.cjs:2](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/consumer.cjs:2).

The CLI takes arguments after the executable and script name. It requires exactly two arguments. Missing either argument, or supplying any extra argument, writes `usage: node cli.cjs STATUS TITLE\n` to stderr and sets exit code 2. Otherwise it writes the formatter result followed by one newline to stdout. Empty string arguments pass this arity check. Unknown status strings also pass and reach the fallback. See [cli.cjs:2](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/cli.cjs:2) and [cli.cjs:7](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/cli.cjs:7). These are traced code paths, not observed process results.

## Where things live

- [format.cjs](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:1) owns status matching, output prefixes, title concatenation, and the named CommonJS export.
- [consumer.cjs](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/consumer.cjs:1) adapts rows to formatter calls.
- [cli.cjs](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/cli.cjs:1) owns argument errors, output streams, and the final newline.
- [package.json](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/package.json:1) declares `node --test` as the test script. File discovery found no tests, consistent with [README.md:6](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/README.md:6).

## Gotchas

Strict comparison means `Queued`, ` queued`, `done `, unknown strings, missing statuses, symbols, and objects all take the fallback. Even a boxed string or object that would convert to `queued` does not match. The existing comparisons do not coerce the status or call its conversion hooks. A lookup through ordinary object properties could accidentally recognize inherited keys such as `constructor`, `toString`, or `__proto__`, or coerce an object key. Preserve the current comparisons' observable behavior when choosing a replacement. This is a static consequence of the equality checks at [format.cjs:3](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:3), not a runtime result.

Every return uses `prefix + title`. Missing titles therefore follow JavaScript's `undefined` concatenation behavior; null, numbers, objects, and symbols follow the same addition rules. Object conversion uses the addition operator's default primitive hint, and conversion errors propagate. A template literal or explicit `String(title)` can differ for some values. Keep this behavior or establish an explicitly narrower input contract before changing it. See [format.cjs:4](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:4) and [format.cjs:21](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:21).

The formatter preserves whitespace and embedded newlines in string titles. Only the CLI adds the final newline, so moving newline handling into the formatter would also change the row consumer. Neither caller catches formatter errors. See [consumer.cjs:2](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/consumer.cjs:2) and [cli.cjs:7](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/cli.cjs:7).

No settings changed and no children were spawned. Evidence is in `03-preflight.stdout`, the numbered command records, and `read-hashes.jsonl` in this directory.

### Language

7. **AI vocabulary.** Additionally, crucial, delve, enduring, enhance, fostering, garner, interplay, intricate, landscape (abstract), pivotal, showcase, tapestry (abstract), testament, underscore, vibrant. Replace with plain words.
8. **Fancy ways to say "is".** "serves as", "stands as", "boasts", "features". Just say "is" or "has".
9. **"Not just X, but Y."** State the point directly instead.
10. **Rule of three.** Forcing ideas into groups of three. Use the natural number.
11. **Synonym cycling.** Protagonist, main character, central figure, hero all in one paragraph. Pick one, repeat it.
12. **False ranges.** "from X to Y" where X and Y aren't on a meaningful scale. List topics directly.

### Style

13. **Em dash overuse.** Avoid em dashes entirely. Use periods or commas only (no parentheses, no en dashes, no hyphen-as-dash substitutes). If a thought needs separation, end the sentence or use a comma.
14. **Colon overuse.** Colons are fine before a list or example. Not as mid-sentence connectors. "If you're coming from traditional automation: instead of registering event handlers, you describe conditions" adds nothing with the colon. Rewrite to let the point stand on its own without comparison framing. "Describing when the scheduler should fire works best as plain English." Same meaning, no crutch punctuation.
15. **Boldface overuse.** Don't bold every proper noun or acronym.
16. **Inline-header lists.** The tell is a bold label and colon that restates the line: "**Performance:** Performance improved...". Convert those to prose. A bold lead-in that ends in a period, names the item, and is followed by genuinely new detail ("**Schema in TypeScript.** Tables live in one file.") is fine, not a tell.
17. **Title case headings.** Use sentence case.
18. **Decorative emojis.** Remove from headings and bullets.
19. **Curly quotes.** Replace with straight quotes.

### Communication artifacts

20. **Chatbot phrases.** "I hope this helps!", "Let me know if...", "Of course!", "Certainly!", "Found the smoking gun!" Remove.
22. **Sycophantic tone.** "Great question! You're absolutely right!" Respond directly.

### Filler

23. **Filler phrases.** "In order to" becomes "To". "Due to the fact that" becomes "Because". "It is important to note that" gets deleted.
24. **Excessive hedging.** "could potentially possibly be argued that it might" becomes "may".
25. **Generic conclusions.** "The future looks bright." State specific plans or facts.

### Jargon

26. **Abstract metaphor nouns.** Substrate, wedge, vector, locus, vantage, nexus, primitive (as noun), harness (as metaphor), surface (as in "API surface"), bedrock, scaffolding (as metaphor), modality, paradigm, gold-plating, ratchet (as metaphor), evacuate (for moving code), endgame, north star, flywheel. These read as technical but usually have a plainer concrete word. "Substrate" becomes "base". "Wedge in" becomes "add". "Vector" becomes "way" or "method". "Gold-plating" becomes "more than the job needs". "Ratchet" becomes the mechanism's real name or "a limit that only tightens". "Evacuate" becomes "move out". "Endgame" becomes "the last phase". Pick the concrete word.

### Plain speech

27. **Say what it does, not how it feels.** "the database stays close at hand", "SQL you can read", "types that follow your schema" name a feeling. The fix names the mechanism or a number: "`.toSQL()` returns the exact string sent to the database", "a column rename fails the build". Ask what the sentence tells the reader to do or know, then write that. If you can't restate it as a concrete instruction, fact, or number, cut it. One more check: if the sentence could appear unchanged in another project's docs, it says nothing about this one. Cut it.
28. **Shorten or split dense sentences.** If the reader has to backtrack to parse a sentence, break it in two or drop clauses. One idea per sentence.
29. **Active voice.** Prefer it. Catch "is/are/was/were + past participle" and name the actor: "queries are validated" becomes "the compiler validates queries", "the file is parsed by the loader" becomes "the loader parses the file". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or genuinely doesn't matter.
30. **Cut adverbs, or use a stronger verb.** "runs quickly" becomes "is fast" or the number. "significantly improves" becomes the measured delta. An adverb propping up a weak verb means the verb is wrong.
31. **Prefer the plain word.** "utilize" becomes "use", "leverage" becomes "use", "facilitate" becomes "help", "numerous" becomes "many", "in the event that" becomes "if". The fancier synonym is rarely clearer.
32. **Mannered prose.** Metaphor or flourish where a literal phrase exists: aphorisms ("wire it or delete it"), rhetorical fragments for effect, personified code ("the plan holds it"), figurative verbs ("rides along", "stands on"), stock framing phrases. "A dial worth turning" becomes "a parameter worth varying". Say what you mean. Rule 26 covers the metaphor nouns.
33. **Over-compression.** Dropped articles, verbless fragments, symbol-speak, and abbreviations that make the reader decode instead of read. "Parser rejects bad date → exit 2, no write" becomes "The parser rejects a bad date, exits with code 2, and writes nothing." Write whole sentences with their articles and verbs, and spell out arrows and abbreviations.

name: jstack-principle-model-the-domain
description: "Apply when writing stateful logic, or when code branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files."
---

# Model the Domain

Encode the real domain in a data structure instead of scattering it across conditionals. A structure that matches the domain makes invalid states unrepresentable and deletes branches. Choosing it at write time is cheap. Recovering it later reads as a refactor and gets deferred.

Reach for:

- A state machine instead of scattered booleans, phases, or lifecycle checks.
- A typed model instead of loose parameters or repeated shape assumptions.
- A map, registry, lookup table, or discriminated union instead of branching spread across files.
- A reducer or command/event model instead of ad hoc state mutations.
- A module organized around one body of domain knowledge instead of a sequence such as load, validate, transform, and save. Execution order is not ownership.
- A small module boundary that gathers repeated behavior, ownership, or invariants.
- A queue, cache, index, graph, tree, or normalized collection where the access pattern calls for it.
- Any other structure that fits. When none fits, work out what the code must never allow and how the data gets read, then find the structure that encodes exactly that.

Do not force an abstraction. Prefer boring code if the current shape is already clear, local, and unlikely to grow. Be skeptical of an abstraction that adds indirection without removing branches, duplicated rules, invalid states, or lifecycle risk.

The sign that you skipped this is a new feature that grows an existing if/else chain by one more branch, or a second boolean that must stay in sync with the first. Temporal decomposition is another sign. Phase-named modules repeat the same domain rules across steps.

Apply within the requested scope and existing authorization, preserving unrelated work and repository constraints. Direct invocation does not activate jstack-juan-mode or change model configuration.

name: jstack-principle-subtract-before-you-add
description: "Apply when sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead code, redundant validators, and stub references first, then build on the simpler base."

# Subtract Before You Add

When evolving a system, remove complexity first, then build. Default to subtraction.

Make simplification a continual investment. Leave the design slightly simpler and more capable behind the same or smaller surface than you found it.

- Sequence removal before construction
- Cut before you polish (get to the minimum before investing in quality)
- Design for observed usage, not speculative edge cases
- No speculative validators, parsers, or guards beyond what the spec demands
- Simplify prompts (remove redundant instructions, excessive templates)
- When a reference has no novel content, delete it rather than leaving a stub

Apply within the requested scope and existing authorization, preserving unrelated work and repository constraints. Direct invocation does not activate jstack-juan-mode or change model configuration.

name: jstack-principle-laziness-protocol
description: "Apply when refactoring, evaluating diff size, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem."
---

# Laziness Protocol

Aim for the most result with the least code and complexity.

- **Prefer deletion.** When asked to refactor or improve, look for removals before additions.
- **Maintain a flat call hierarchy.** Avoid deep call chains. A rich interface that hides substantial work is not a deep call chain. If answering a question requires tracing through more than 3 files or layers, flatten it.
- **Consolidate decisions.** Do not repeat the same choice in several places. Put it behind one source of truth and pass the result as a simple flag.
- **Minimize the diff.** Make the smallest change that solves the problem. Fewer lines beat "elegant" boilerplate.
- **Question the threading.** If a task asks you to pass a new signal through types, schemas, pipelines, or similar layers, stop and look for a more direct path.
- **Sweat the small leaks.** Remove tiny pass-throughs, representation leaks, and duplicated choices before they spread. Small leaks compound into permanent coordination costs.

**The test:** If a human developer would find the code exhausting to maintain, it is a bad solution.

Apply within the requested scope and existing authorization, preserving unrelated work and repository constraints. Direct invocation does not activate jstack-juan-mode or change model configuration.

name: jstack-principle-prove-it-works
description: "Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'"
---

# Prove It Works

Verify every task output by checking the real thing directly. Do not infer from proxies, self-reports, or "it compiles."

**Why:** Unverified work has unknown correctness. Indirect verification (file mtimes, output freshness, agent self-reports, cached screenshots) feels cheaper than direct observation. Acting on a wrong inference costs far more than checking the source.

Check the real thing, not a proxy:

- Check process liveness directly, not indirectly through derived state
- Read the actual value, not a cached or derived representation
- When verification fails, suspect the observation method before suspecting the system

## Script the check when you can

The strongest proof is a deterministic script that re-runs the same comparison, not a one-time eyeball. Write the script, run it, and keep its output as an artifact a reviewer can re-run instead of trusting your word.

Keep the artifact visible for the human. Commit it only for large or complex work where the trail has to be auditable later, like a big port or migration (the **jstack-show-me-your-work** skill).

name: jstack-principle-sequence-verifiable-units
description: "Apply to multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and to how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a verifiable state, check each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself to a reviewer."
---

# Sequence work into verifiable units

Order work as a sequence of small units, each ending in a state you can check, and don't advance until the current one is green.

**Why:** A break caught at the unit that caused it is cheap to localize. A break caught after a batch is buried, and you have already built further on a broken base. Sequencing those same units into a delivery a reviewer can replay turns "trust me" into "watch it go red, then green."

**Execution.** In a sweep, migration, or any run of similar edits, verify each change before starting the next. Each unit is a before/after bracket: known-good state, one change, run the check, then proceed. Establish a known baseline first so every check measures against it. Preserve existing work; use an isolated checkout when needed rather than automatically rebasing a dirty or shared branch. When a lever does the edits, the per-unit check is nearly free. Run it anyway.

**Delivery.** Stack commits and PRs in the order that proves the work. The canonical shape is the failing test first, then the fix on top. Other story orders are a subtraction before the reshape, a baseline capture before the treatment, the scaffold before the feature. Each delivery unit must pass its required checks before landing, and the sequence reads as an argument. Preserve failing-test evidence without presenting a red commit as independently merge-ready. Merging remains separately authorized.

The sequencing complement to the **prove-it-works** principle skill, which keeps each check real, and the **build-the-lever** principle skill, which makes the per-unit check cheap.

Verify jstack identity when available and report ambiguity. If a required helper is unavailable, report the missing dependency and incomplete procedure, continue independent authorized work, and leave installation to the user.

### Refactoring

**You own the contract. The structure changes. The behavior does not.** Distinct from Feature, which adds behavior, and Bug fix, which corrects it.

If the cleanup reveals a missing feature or a real bug, split it out and ship the structural change first against the pinned contract. A redesign is allowed, but name it and route to Feature. Large or cross-cutting structural work belongs to the **jstack-figure-it-out** skill. This playbook is the focused-to-medium change.

1. Pin the behavior contract first. Run the **jstack-how** skill over the affected subsystem to learn the contract, then write a characterization test, snapshot, or equivalence harness that captures current behavior before any structure moves. If the area has no coverage, write the pin before touching structure. Type check and lint are not a pin. Discover the helper and pass its configured roles, source scope and selected absolute configuration through the mode's preflight.
2. Name the structure the code is missing per **jstack-principle-model-the-domain**. Boring code stays when the shape is already clear and local. The reshape must delete branches or invalid states, not add indirection.
3. Name the target shape. State what the module layout, types, and call graph should be if built today (**jstack-principle-foundational-thinking**, **jstack-principle-redesign-from-first-principles**). If the target crosses a function boundary, run the **jstack-architect** skill for parallel design exploration of the shape before the move, returning a design before step 5. Preserve its configured panel and two structurally distinct candidate requirement; an undersized panel or unavailable helper leaves this step incomplete, without adding seats.
4. Subtract before you add. Delete dead code, collapse one-caller wrappers, drop redundant validators, and remove orphan references before introducing the new shape (**jstack-principle-subtract-before-you-add**). The smallest change that reaches the target shape ships (**jstack-principle-laziness-protocol**). A speculative cleanup that "might help" gets reverted.
5. Move in small behavior-preserving steps, each keeping the pin green. For API reshapes, migrate every caller and delete the old API in the same wave (**jstack-principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis**). No compatibility shims, no parallel old-and-new paths. Spot-check every rename against the actual files. Renames silently miss usages in strings, prose, and back-references. Delegate the mechanical edits to a subagent using the configured `feature, refactoring` role, or `hardest tasks` when warranted by the mode's difficulty rule, with a specific scope (file paths, the names being moved, the behavior to hold). Resolve through the mode's preflight and retain the selected absolute configuration; no fixed-model fallback.
6. Prove behavior is unchanged on the real artifact, not "it compiles" (**jstack-principle-prove-it-works**). For larger reshapes, run an equivalence check: a script that diffs old-vs-new outputs, a recorded baseline replayed against the new code, or a smoke run on the matching surface via the relevant control skill. Discover the matching helper, including `jstack-control-cli` for terminal apps. Inspect the delegated diff and run the public equivalence checks yourself; retain actual output and unmet prerequisites. Missing access or wrong-surface proof is incomplete.
7. Confirm the change is worth keeping. The success measure is reduced reader load (**jstack-principle-minimize-reader-load**). If the diff does not lower reader load somewhere, revert it.
8. Rebase into small ordered commits. A subtraction commit, then the reshape, then any follow-on cleanup. Shape them with the **jstack-principle-sequence-verifiable-units** principle skill, so each behavior-preserving slice stays green before the next. Commit and rebase only within the task's authority and preserve unrelated work; for uncommitted local delivery, retain verified artifacts and the proposed order. Run **Opening a PR** when publication is authorized. That procedure remains unavailable in this package; disclose the gap rather than claiming it ran. This playbook does not authorize merging or installation.

**Reply:** the structure that changed, the pin you held it against, the equivalence proof, the reader-load delta, what shipped and what got reverted. No new behavior.

# Configuration discovery and resolution

Find `jstack-setup` in the executing provider's available skill catalog and expand its advertised `SKILL.md` path. Read its configuration contract relative to that installation. Pass the entrypoint's parent directory to `--setup-skill`; its directory need not share a parent with `jstack-juan-mode`. Do not search arbitrary repositories for a convenient resolver or copy `models.py`. A missing installation is a dependency error with manual installation as the remedy.

Call live `orchestrator_capabilities` and write the unwrapped payload to a task-owned temporary JSON file. Read the installed setup skill's T3 Code integration reference for catalog capture, lazy discovery and the supported ACP transport. Record its observation time with task evidence, refresh it for each new routed task, and refresh again after a dispatch rejection that might indicate catalog drift. Remove temporary catalog files when no longer needed.

Run the preflight from any working directory using absolute paths:

```sh
python3 /path/to/jstack-juan-mode/scripts/preflight.py \
  --setup-skill /discovered/path/to/jstack-setup \
  --project-root /path/to/target-project \
  --catalog /task-owned/path/catalog.json \
  --role 'how explorer'
```

Setup-jstack's configuration contract owns lookup. The preflight passes `--config` and `--project-root` to its canonical `models.py resolve --with-source` command, then reports the selected absolute `config` path and `configSource`. Precedence is explicit file, `JSTACK_CONFIG`, an existing project `.jstack/models.json`, then global defaults. The selected file supplies all 17 roles; malformed or incomplete project settings produce an error. The preflight does not initialize, repair or save configuration. An error in another role still prevents execution. On error, report the file and role or dependency, and let jstack-setup handle a user-requested repair.

Pass the task's known project root explicitly when the current directory belongs to another checkout or the installed skill. Without `--project-root`, the canonical helper discovers the caller's Git checkout root. Before dispatch or a checkout change, retain the returned absolute `config` path and supply it as `--config` for children and later phases of that task. Re-read and validate that file; do not rediscover from a child's worktree, where an untracked project configuration may be absent. A new task repeats project lookup. An installed jstack-setup that lacks the shared lookup CLI requires a manual update; do not fall back to a second lookup implementation.

Each returned `targets` entry is either a concrete T3 Code target or JSON `null`. Pass concrete targets unchanged, including their options. For `null`, omit `target` to preserve the current parent's provider, model and effort. The helper reports the effective inherited identity only for capability checks; that identity is not a replacement target and does not establish model-family diversity. Read current thread configuration when effective options matter to evidence.

## Role and fan-out semantics

Use `feature, refactoring`, `bug-fix`, `perf-issue` and `hillclimb` for their implementation routes. Use `hardest tasks` for a task whose difficulty needs that configured role. Delegated prose and judgment use `judgment and prose`. Helpers declare their existing configuration role keys, such as `how explorer` and `swarm workers`. The `jstack-` skill prefix does not rename configuration roles. For a step with no dedicated role, declare the relevant existing role or keep the work in the parent.

Preserve every configured list entry in order, including repeated and inherited selections. `architect runners`, `arena runners` and `interrogate reviewers` are panels. `arena cross-judge pool` supplies alternatives; the procedure selects one eligible judge, not the entire pool. `swarm workers` supplies a model default, not a worker count. The preflight reports these three selection kinds so callers cannot confuse alternatives with fan-out.

The `availability` array aligns with `targets` by index. A pool alternative with `canDispatch: false` remains in the output with its reason; select only executable alternatives that also meet the procedure's independence requirement. A pool with no executable alternative fails. Scalar and panel roles require every selected seat to execute. This capability handling does not relax whole-map validation of saved provider, model or option selections.

Before dispatch, check the procedure's required count and independence against the effective selections. One inherited seat is a valid configuration, but does not satisfy a two-candidate design or a different-family judge requirement. Report the exact unmet requirement. Retain existing choices until the user authorizes an adjustment; do not invent extra models or increase fan-out.

# Execution contract

Use the current tool schemas and injected T3 Code instructions. Prefer native same-provider children when they support the resolved model, options and required lifecycle. Use T3 Code `delegate_task` for cross-provider work, selections the native tool cannot express, or explicitly T3 Code-owned children. Catalog presence and preflight success are prerequisites, not proof a provider ran successfully.

## Child brief and lifecycle

Supply the following in every child brief because T3 Code delegation does not copy the parent conversation:

- Original goal, later constraints, relevant findings and selected procedure.
- For ordinary playbook children, the discovered absolute mode path with an explicit full-read requirement and applicable principle leaves; specialized workflow children keep their own briefs.
- Absolute checkout path, base revision, owned paths and read-only or write scope.
- The parent's selected absolute model-config path, passed explicitly to preflight in the child.
- Permitted commands or actions where the task needs a narrow boundary.
- Output location, observable acceptance checks and the evidence to return.
- Review findings and unresolved objections when this is a new review round.
- Stop condition and actions reserved for the parent.

For T3 Code dispatch, choose a distinct `clientRequestId` per logical round and reuse it only when retrying that dispatch. Retain the returned `taskId`; `childThreadId` is backing storage, not a target for continuing review. Every new task, follow-up, fix, retry or queue item uses a fresh child and consolidated brief by default. A non-review continuation requires named expensive live state that cannot reasonably move; a running child may receive stop/hold instructions without becoming a new work round. Each T3 review round always uses a fresh `delegate_task` with the consolidated brief. Use completion delivery and `task_status` when needed mid-task. A wait timeout does not cancel work, and a completed turn with pending child runs is not task completion.

Before replacing or abandoning a task, cancel its owned child work and reconcile any writes. Never give the same writable scope to a replacement while the original can still write. Inspect actual artifacts and verification output before accepting a child summary. Record task ID, effective selection, checkout, revision, permitted scope, outcome and evidence in the task's existing handoff when the work needs recovery.

## Workspaces

A child that needs a separate checkout uses T3 Code `delegate_task` with `isolation: "worktree"`, across any provider or model. It starts from the parent's local commit and completes project setup before the child runs; uncommitted edits are not copied. Ensure the intended base and required inputs are committed or provided as explicit read-only artifacts before dispatch. Do not simulate app binding by asking a child to create or change to a worktree in its prompt. Do not create a commit merely to dispatch if committing is outside the task's scope.

Retain the returned task identity and inspect the actual assigned checkout, branch, base revision, edits and verification before accepting the result. Keep shared plan files parent-owned and ports, logs and mutable build outputs separate. Separate checkouts do not by themselves prove every provider/editor's behavior. When a separate checkout is unnecessary, a shared checkout is valid for bounded reads or serial writes; concurrent writers require disjoint ownership and demonstrated tool behavior.

Parallel read-only work can proceed within its scope. Independent top-level conversations use `t3_thread_launch` only when the user requests them, with an explicit workspace strategy. Creating a top-level conversation is not a workaround for child isolation.

## PRs and verification

The parent links every worked PR with T3 Code. The parent also owns PR watches and wake handling; children return results instead of watching. Read existing comments before watching, dispatch fresh work for new findings, and stop watching when handing responsibility back to the user. Check readiness against the current PR head and forge state before any authorized merge.

Keep task delivery separate from mode activation. An implementation request does not itself authorize merging, publishing unrelated messages, installing skills or recurring schedules. Use already-granted authority without repeated confirmation. Preserve local user work and report incomplete verification accurately.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Resolve a jstack role through its discovered setup skill without dispatching."""

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
import re
import subprocess
import sys


def preflight(setup_skill, config, catalog_path, role, project_root=None):
    setup = Path(setup_skill).expanduser().resolve()
    entry = (setup / "SKILL.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    frontmatter = entry.split("---", 2)
    if (not entry.startswith("---\n") or len(frontmatter) != 3
            or not re.search(r'^name:\s*[\'\"]?jstack-setup[\'\"]?\s*$',
                             frontmatter[1], re.MULTILINE)):
        raise ValueError("--setup-skill must be the catalog-discovered jstack-setup directory")
    resolver = setup / "scripts" / "models.py"
    if not resolver.is_file():
        raise ValueError(f"missing jstack-setup resolver: {resolver}")
    command = [sys.executable, str(resolver), "resolve"]
    if config is not None:
        command.append(str(config))
    command.extend(["--catalog", str(catalog_path), "--role", role, "--with-source"])
    if project_root is not None:
        command.extend(["--project-root", str(project_root)])
    result = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
    if result.returncode:
        if result.returncode == 2:
            raise ValueError("jstack-setup rejected the CLI arguments; check the role and manually "
                             "update jstack-setup if it lacks shared lookup:\n" + result.stderr.strip())
        raise ValueError(result.stderr.strip() or "jstack-setup resolution failed")
    resolved = json.loads(result.stdout)
    targets = resolved["targets"]
    if not isinstance(targets, list) or not targets:
        raise ValueError("jstack-setup returned no ordered targets")
    catalog = json.loads(Path(catalog_path).expanduser().read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    parent = catalog.get("inheritedProviderInstanceId")
    providers = {p["providerInstanceId"]: p for p in catalog["providers"]}
    kind = ("pool" if role == "arena cross-judge pool" else "panel"
            if role in {"arena runners", "architect runners", "interrogate reviewers"}
            else "scalar")
    identities, availability = [], []
    for target in targets:
        inherited = target is None
        pid = parent if inherited else target["providerInstanceId"]
        model = catalog.get("inheritedModel") if inherited else target["model"]
        provider = providers.get(pid)
        reason = None
        if (not provider or provider.get("canRunChildTask") is not True
                or not model or model not in {m["id"] for m in provider.get("models", [])}):
            reason = f"effective child selection unavailable: {pid!r}/{model!r}"
        elif pid != parent and provider.get("canRunCrossProviderChildTask") is not True:
            reason = f"cross-provider child execution unavailable on {pid!r}"
        if reason and kind != "pool":
            raise ValueError(f"{role}: {reason}")
        identities.append({"providerInstanceId": pid, "model": model, "inherited": inherited})
        availability.append({"canDispatch": reason is None, "reason": reason})
    if kind == "pool" and not any(seat["canDispatch"] for seat in availability):
        reasons = "; ".join(seat["reason"] for seat in availability)
        raise ValueError(f"{role}: no executable judge alternative: {reasons}")
    return {"role": role, "selectionKind": kind, "targets": targets,
            "effectiveIdentities": identities, "availability": availability,
            "resolver": str(resolver),
            "config": resolved["config"], "configSource": resolved["configSource"]}


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--setup-skill", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--catalog", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--role", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--config")
    parser.add_argument("--project-root")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    try:
        result = preflight(args.setup_skill, args.config, args.catalog, args.role, args.project_root)
        print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    except (ValueError, OSError, KeyError, TypeError) as error:
        parser.exit(1, f"jstack-juan-mode: {error}\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# T3 Code integration

Use the actual callable tool schemas and injected T3 Code instructions as authority. Tool names may have a harness prefix such as `mcp__t3_code__`.

- `orchestrator_capabilities` discovers provider instances, model IDs, options and inheritance. It is the validation source, not a model list copied into this skill.
- `delegate_task` creates parent-owned work. Concrete seats become `target` with `providerInstanceId`, `model` and `options`. Inherited seats omit `target`. Retain returned task IDs; use fresh delegated tasks for new review rounds with consolidated briefs and distinct retry-stable request IDs. Prefer asynchronous completion delivery over polling.

# Task status formatter

## Overview

`formatStatus(status, title)` returns a status prefix followed by the title. It is the single formatter used by both the row consumer and the command line interface. The CommonJS module exports an object containing `formatStatus`. See [format.cjs:1](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:1), [format.cjs:23](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:23), [consumer.cjs:1](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/consumer.cjs:1), and [cli.cjs:1](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/cli.cjs:1).

This explanation comes from static reading at revision `eb4203be1362f6d924dc53d35aeac9a0dfe60240`. I gathered the evidence directly, without explorers. I did not execute the formatter, launch the application, or run tests. The supplied README explicitly requires compatible status spellings, output bytes, case handling, and argument errors. See [README.md:5](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/README.md:5).

## Key concepts

The status is compared with six primitive strings using strict equality. There is no validation, normalization, trimming, or case conversion. The title is appended with JavaScript string addition. The function returns no trailing newline. See [format.cjs:3](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:3) through the fallback at [format.cjs:21](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:21).

| Exact status | Prefix, including its final space | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `queued` | `'[WAIT] '` | [format.cjs:4](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:4) |
| `active` | `'[RUN] '` | [format.cjs:7](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:7) |
| `paused` | `'[HOLD] '` | [format.cjs:10](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:10) |
| `done` | `'[OK] '` | [format.cjs:13](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:13) |
| `failed` | `'[FAIL] '` | [format.cjs:16](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:16) |
| `cancelled` | `'[STOP] '` | [format.cjs:19](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:19) |
| Any other value | `'[?] '` | [format.cjs:21](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:21) |

## How it works

Each call checks the status in source order and immediately returns the matching prefix plus the title. If no comparison succeeds, it returns the fallback prefix plus the title. The local `unusedPrefix` constant has no use in the module. See [format.cjs:2](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:2).

The row consumer exports a function that calls `rows.map`. For each row it reads `row.status` and `row.title`, then passes both values directly to the formatter. Ordinary arrays therefore produce formatted strings in row order, and sparse arrays retain the usual `map` behavior. The consumer does not validate rows or catch errors. See [consumer.cjs:2](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/consumer.cjs:2).

The CLI takes arguments after the executable and script name. It requires exactly two arguments. Missing either argument, or supplying any extra argument, writes `usage: node cli.cjs STATUS TITLE\n` to stderr and sets exit code 2. Otherwise it writes the formatter result followed by one newline to stdout. Empty string arguments pass this arity check. Unknown status strings also pass and reach the fallback. See [cli.cjs:2](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/cli.cjs:2) and [cli.cjs:7](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/cli.cjs:7). These are traced code paths, not observed process results.

## Where things live

- [format.cjs](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:1) owns status matching, output prefixes, title concatenation, and the named CommonJS export.
- [consumer.cjs](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/consumer.cjs:1) adapts rows to formatter calls.
- [cli.cjs](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/cli.cjs:1) owns argument errors, output streams, and the final newline.
- [package.json](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/package.json:1) declares `node --test` as the test script. File discovery found no tests, consistent with [README.md:6](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/README.md:6).

## Gotchas

Strict comparison means `Queued`, ` queued`, `done `, unknown strings, missing statuses, symbols, and objects all take the fallback. Even a boxed string or object that would convert to `queued` does not match. The existing comparisons do not coerce the status or call its conversion hooks. A lookup through ordinary object properties could accidentally recognize inherited keys such as `constructor`, `toString`, or `__proto__`, or coerce an object key. Preserve the current comparisons' observable behavior when choosing a replacement. This is a static consequence of the equality checks at [format.cjs:3](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:3), not a runtime result.

Every return uses `prefix + title`. Missing titles therefore follow JavaScript's `undefined` concatenation behavior; null, numbers, objects, and symbols follow the same addition rules. Object conversion uses the addition operator's default primitive hint, and conversion errors propagate. A template literal or explicit `String(title)` can differ for some values. Keep this behavior or establish an explicitly narrower input contract before changing it. See [format.cjs:4](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:4) and [format.cjs:21](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/format.cjs:21).

The formatter preserves whitespace and embedded newlines in string titles. Only the CLI adds the final newline, so moving newline handling into the formatter would also change the row consumer. Neither caller catches formatter errors. See [consumer.cjs:2](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/consumer.cjs:2) and [cli.cjs:7](/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/cli.cjs:7).

The caller search covered all five discovered project files using `rg` with the terms `format|require|exports|status`. It found two callers in this snapshot. External consumers are unknown. No runtime compatibility checks were authorized in this phase; the coordinator still needs to verify exact outputs, CLI streams and exit codes, export compatibility, and the status/title coercion boundaries before and after the refactor.

Preflight passed for `how explainer` using the explicit configuration and a fresh live catalog. It resolved to `null`, with inherited `codex/gpt-6-astra`, and reported `canDispatch: true`. No settings changed and no children were spawned. Evidence is in `03-preflight.stdout`, the numbered command records, and `read-hashes.jsonl` in this directory.

## Intent

Simplify the repetitive formatter while preserving its current behavior in a focused local refactor. Review both candidate structures before implementation.

## Reviewers

- Reviewer A inherited codex/gpt-6-astra and returned no findings.
- Reviewer B inherited codex/gpt-6-astra and returned no findings.

## Act on

None.

## Consider

None.

## Noted

Both reviewers demonstrated that replacing Map.prototype.get changes candidate A's behavior. Candidate A documents its native Map assumption. Neither fixture caller replaces built-ins. Treat that as an explicit environmental limit, not a supported-input regression. Runtime equivalence on the final artifact remains required.

## Dismissed

Neither six direct comparisons nor one private map is itself a concrete maintainability defect. The selection remains a bounded design judgment. No new abstraction or API is warranted.

## Agreement map

Both inherited reviewers found no ordinary-input defect and independently confirmed the changed-built-in distinction. This is corroboration from separate contexts, not model diversity. Input hashes remained stable, all children are terminal, and the two disposable probe sets passed. The probe counts describe different input sets and are not additive measures of coverage.

## Lead judgment

Keep candidate A as the implementation base because the requested simplification is a finite mapping and the Refactoring shape criterion favors deleting branches. The map removes the repeated control flow while retaining one local module and the public function. The Arena judge's preference for candidate B is retained in judge/verdict.md. No reviewer found a correctness reason to overrule either design. The original six-test pin and old-versus-new checks will decide implementation acceptance.

**You own the contract. The structure changes. The behavior does not.** Distinct from Feature, which adds behavior, and Bug fix, which corrects it.

If the cleanup reveals a missing feature or a real bug, split it out and ship the structural change first against the pinned contract. A redesign is allowed, but name it and route to Feature. Large or cross-cutting structural work belongs to the **jstack-figure-it-out** skill. This playbook is the focused-to-medium change.

1. Pin the behavior contract first. Run the **jstack-how** skill over the affected subsystem to learn the contract, then write a characterization test, snapshot, or equivalence harness that captures current behavior before any structure moves. If the area has no coverage, write the pin before touching structure. Type check and lint are not a pin. Discover the helper and pass its configured roles, source scope and selected absolute configuration through the mode's preflight.
2. Name the structure the code is missing per **jstack-principle-model-the-domain**. Boring code stays when the shape is already clear and local. The reshape must delete branches or invalid states, not add indirection.
3. Name the target shape. State what the module layout, types, and call graph should be if built today (**jstack-principle-foundational-thinking**, **jstack-principle-redesign-from-first-principles**). 4. Subtract before you add. Delete dead code, collapse one-caller wrappers, drop redundant validators, and remove orphan references before introducing the new shape (**jstack-principle-subtract-before-you-add**). The smallest change that reaches the target shape ships (**jstack-principle-laziness-protocol**). A speculative cleanup that "might help" gets reverted.

import errno,json,os,pathlib,pty,select,subprocess,sys,time

root=pathlib.Path('/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-evidence')
results=[]
for args,expected,code in [(['active','Build'],b'[RUN] Build\r\n',0),([],b'usage: node cli.cjs STATUS TITLE\r\n',2),(['Done',''],b'[?] \r\n',0)]:
    master,slave=pty.openpty()
    child=subprocess.Popen(['node','/tmp/jstack-refactoring-20261016/two-seat-app/cli.cjs',*args],stdin=slave,stdout=slave,stderr=slave,env={**os.environ,'TERM':'dumb','NO_COLOR':'1'})
    os.close(slave)
    output=b''
    try:
        deadline=time.monotonic()+5
        while time.monotonic()<deadline:
            ready,_,_=select.select([master],[],[],0.1)
            if ready:
                try: part=os.read(master,4096)
                except OSError as error:
                    if error.errno==errno.EIO: break
                    raise
                if not part: break
                output+=part
            elif child.poll() is not None: break
        child.wait(timeout=1)
        assert output==expected,(args,output,expected)
        assert child.returncode==code,(args,child.returncode,code)
        results.append({'args':args,'terminalOutput':output.decode(),'exit':child.returncode})
    finally:
        if child.poll() is None:
            child.kill()
            child.wait()
        os.close(master)
text=json.dumps(results,indent=2)
(root/('terminal-'+sys.argv[1]+'.json')).write_text(text+'\n')
print(text)
